questions.q: What is the index of the first element in an Apex List?
questions.explain: A list is an ordered collection distinguished by indices, and the index position of the first element in a list is always 0.

questions.q: Can a Set contain duplicate elements?
options: Yes, up to two duplicates per value
No -- a set does not contain any duplicates
Only if the elements are sObjects
Yes, sets behave exactly like lists
questions.explain: A set is defined as an unordered collection of elements that do not contain any duplicates; adding an existing value again has no effect.

questions.q: What happens when you put() a new value into a Map using a key that already exists?
options: The map silently ignores the new value and keeps the old one
The existing entry for that key is overwritten with the new value
The map grows to store both values under that key
questions.explain: Adding a map entry with a key that matches an existing key overwrites the existing entry for that key with the new entry.

questions.q: Which method returns a Set containing all of the keys currently stored in a Map?
questions.explain: keySet() returns a set that contains all of the keys in the map, as shown when retrieving the set of all keys after a few put() calls.

questions.q: Why can't you access a Set element using an index like mySet.get(0)?
options: Sets don't support a get method at all for any purpose
A set is an unordered collection -- you can't access a set element at a specific index, only iterate over it
Set elements are always sorted alphabetically instead of indexed
Only Maps support indexed access, not Lists or Sets
questions.explain: A set is an unordered collection, so you can't access a set element at a specific index; you can only iterate over set elements or check membership with contains().
